item.title: “Here, Mahānāma, a noble disciple dwells with aroused energy, abandoning unwholesome states and acquiring wholesome states, steadfast, vigorous, not shirking the burden of wholesome states.…
item.description:
“Here, Mahānāma, a noble disciple dwells with aroused energy, abandoning unwholesome states and acquiring wholesome states, steadfast, vigorous, not shirking the burden of wholesome states. He has mindfulness, endowed with supreme mindfulness and discernment, recollecting and recalling what was done and said long ago. He has wisdom, endowed with wisdom regarding arising and passing away, noble and penetrating, leading to the complete destruction of suffering. Thus, Mahānāma, a noble disciple is endowed with noble qualities.”

From: Majjhima Nikāya 53 – Sekhasutta

item.title: Standing to one side, the deity Sudatta recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One: As if struck by a sword, As if…
item.description:
Standing to one side, the deity Sudatta recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One:
As if struck by a sword,
As if fire blazed on the head —
A mindful monk should go forth,
Abandoning lust for sensual pleasures.

(The Blessed One):
As if struck by a sword,
As if fire blazed on the head —
A mindful monk should go forth,
Abandoning identity view.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 2.16

item.title: Venerable Kappa: “For those standing in the middle of the flood, In the terrifying current of existence, Overcome by old age and death — Tell…
item.description:
Venerable Kappa:
“For those standing in the middle of the flood,
In the terrifying current of existence,
Overcome by old age and death —
Tell me, sir, an island,
That there may be no further suffering.”

The Blessed One replied to Kappa:
“For those standing in the middle of the flood,
In the terrifying current of existence,
Overcome by old age and death —
I will tell you, Kappa, an island.

This island is unique —
Possessing nothing, not clinging —
I call it Nibbāna,
The destruction of old age and death.

Knowing this, mindful,
Attaining Nibbāna in this very life,
They do not come into Māra’s power,
Do not become servants of Māra.”

From: Sutta Nipāta 5.11

item.title: “Monks, you should train thus: ‘Our minds will be trained and accumulated as when we went forth; unarisen unwholesome states will not overcome our minds…
item.description:
“Monks, you should train thus: ‘Our minds will be trained and accumulated as when we went forth; unarisen unwholesome states will not overcome our minds and persist; our minds will be trained and accumulated with the perception of impermanence; our minds will be trained and accumulated with the perception of not-self; our minds will be trained and accumulated with the perception of foulness; our minds will be trained and accumulated with the perception of peril; having known the world’s even and uneven, our minds will be trained and accumulated with that perception; having known the world’s arising and passing away, our minds will be trained and accumulated with that perception; having known the world’s origination and cessation, our minds will be trained and accumulated with that perception; our minds will be trained and accumulated with the perception of abandoning; our minds will be trained and accumulated with the perception of dispassion; our minds will be trained and accumulated with the perception of cessation.’ Thus, monks, you should train.”

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 10.59

item.title: “Cunda, I do not teach merely for the sake of preventing defilements in the present life. Cunda, I do not teach the Dhamma only for…
item.description:
“Cunda, I do not teach merely for the sake of preventing defilements in the present life. Cunda, I do not teach the Dhamma only for the sake of eradicating defilements in the future. Cunda, I teach the Dhamma both for preventing defilements in the present life and for eradicating defilements in the future.”

From: Dīgha Nikāya 29 – Pāsādikasutta
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “What do you think, Māgandiya? Have you ever seen or heard of a king or a king’s minister who, while enjoying the five strands of…
item.description:
“What do you think, Māgandiya? Have you ever seen or heard of a king or a king’s minister who, while enjoying the five strands of sensual pleasure fully and completely, without abandoning craving for sensual pleasures, without removing the fever of sensual pleasures, has dwelt, dwells, or will dwell with craving cut off and mind inwardly peaceful?”
“No, Master Gotama.”

From: Majjhima Nikāya 75 – Māgandiyasutta

item.title: “Monks, for any monk or nun whose greed is not abandoned, whose hatred is not abandoned, whose delusion is not abandoned — that one is…
item.description:
“Monks, for any monk or nun whose greed is not abandoned, whose hatred is not abandoned, whose delusion is not abandoned — that one is called one who has not crossed the ocean with its waves, its whirlpools, its sharks, its demons.

But, monks, for any monk or nun whose greed is abandoned, whose hatred is abandoned, whose delusion is abandoned — that one is called one who has crossed the ocean with its waves, its whirlpools, its sharks, its demons, who has crossed to the far shore, a brahmin standing on dry land.

One who has abandoned greed, hatred, and delusion
Has crossed this ocean with its sharks, demons,
Its terrifying waves — so very hard to cross —
He has passed beyond all bonds.

He has abandoned death,
Without attachments,
He has abandoned suffering,
With no further becoming.
Having reached the goal, he is immeasurable —
I say such a one
Has blinded the King of Death.”

From: Itivuttaka 69
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Venerable sir, thus a person has no stain and truly knows: ‘There is no stain in me.’ For such a person, it can be expected:…
item.description:
“Venerable sir, thus a person has no stain and truly knows: ‘There is no stain in me.’ For such a person, it can be expected: ‘He will not attend to the sign of the beautiful. By not attending to the sign of the beautiful, greed will not pollute his mind. He will die without greed, without ill-will, without delusion, without stain, his mind unpolluted.’”

From: Majjhima Nikāya 5 – Anaṅgaṇasutta

item.title: Elder Nun Abhirūpa Nandā: Nandā, look at this body — A collection of many diseases, impure, Full of stench, rotting. Develop your mind, Contemplate the…
item.description:
Elder Nun Abhirūpa Nandā:

Nandā, look at this body —
A collection of many diseases, impure,
Full of stench, rotting.
Develop your mind,
Contemplate the nature of foulness,
Achieve one-pointedness,
With mind well concentrated.

Practice the signless,
Abandon the underlying tendency to conceit.
By fully understanding conceit,
You will live at peace.

From: Therīgāthā 2.1

item.title: “Here, monks, a monk reflects, reflects thus: ‘The various sufferings of many kinds that arise in the world, such as aging and death — what…
item.description:
“Here, monks, a monk reflects, reflects thus: ‘The various sufferings of many kinds that arise in the world, such as aging and death — what is their cause, what is their origin, what gives them birth, what brings them into existence? When what exists does aging and death come to be? When what does not exist does aging and death not come to be?’

Reflecting thus, he understands: ‘The various sufferings of many kinds that arise in the world, such as aging and death — birth is their cause, birth is their origin, birth gives them birth, birth brings them into existence. When birth exists, aging and death come to be. When birth does not exist, aging and death do not come to be.’”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 12.51
